top_stories.title: Want to understand the current state of AI? Check out these charts.
top_stories.summary: MIT Technology Review presents a data-driven overview of where AI stands today, using key charts to illustrate trends in model capabilities, adoption, investment, and societal impact. The piece serves as a broad orientation to the current AI landscape for readers tracking the technology's trajectory. It draws on recent benchmarks, industry data, and research findings to contextualise the pace of change.

top_stories.title: Enterprises power agentic workflows in Cloudflare Agent Cloud with OpenAI
top_stories.summary: OpenAI and Cloudflare have announced a partnership enabling enterprises to build and deploy agentic AI workflows through Cloudflare's Agent Cloud infrastructure. The collaboration is aimed at helping businesses integrate OpenAI models into scalable, production-ready automation pipelines. The announcement signals growing enterprise demand for agentic AI infrastructure from major cloud providers.

top_stories.title: AI plagiarised research that passed checks meant to spot it - then I recognised it was my work
top_stories.summary: A researcher describes discovering that AI-generated content had plagiarised their own academic work and successfully passed plagiarism detection tools designed to catch such copying. The case highlights critical failures in AI detection systems and raises serious concerns about research integrity in academic publishing. The incident underscores the growing challenge institutions face in identifying AI-assisted misconduct.

top_stories.title: The AI Layoff Trap
top_stories.summary: A paper on arXiv examines the dynamic by which companies use AI adoption as justification for workforce reductions, while finding that the productivity gains often fail to materialise as promised. The research explores the economic and organisational consequences of AI-driven layoff decisions and questions the assumptions underlying them. It contributes to the debate around AI's real-world impact on employment.

top_stories.title: Mark Zuckerberg is reportedly building an AI clone to replace him in meetings
top_stories.summary: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg is reported to be developing a personalised AI version of himself capable of attending and participating in meetings on his behalf, according to The Verge. The initiative reflects a broader trend among senior executives experimenting with AI-powered digital avatars for professional delegation. It raises questions about authenticity, decision-making accountability, and the future of executive communication.

further_links.title: Microsoft is testing OpenClaw-like AI bots for 365 Copilot
further_links.summary: Microsoft is piloting autonomous AI agent bots within its 365 Copilot suite, modelled on approaches similar to OpenAI's operator-style agent frameworks.

further_links.title: Sam Altman reportedly targeted in second attack
further_links.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman was reportedly targeted in a second separate security incident, adding to concerns about the safety of high-profile AI executives.

further_links.title: AI Agents Are Coming for Your Dating Life
further_links.summary: Wired examines the growing use of AI agents in online dating, from automated messaging to AI-powered matchmaking tools that act on users' behalf.

further_links.title: Xero & Anthropic fuel AI battle in finance software
further_links.summary: Accounting platform Xero has partnered with Anthropic to integrate Claude into its financial software, intensifying competition among AI-powered business finance tools.

further_links.title: The AI code wars are heating up
further_links.summary: The Verge surveys the intensifying competition between OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic to dominate the AI-assisted coding market as developer tools become a key battleground.

further_links.title: Import AI 453: Breaking AI agents; MirrorCode; and ten views on gradual disempowerment
further_links.summary: Jack Clark's Import AI newsletter covers new research on vulnerabilities in AI agent systems, introduces the MirrorCode project, and surveys ten perspectives on the gradual disempowerment risk from advanced AI.

further_links.title: The Internet's Most Powerful Archiving Tool Is in Peril
further_links.summary: Wired reports on serious threats facing a major internet archiving service, with implications for digital preservation, research, and access to historical web content.

further_links.title: European AI. A playbook to own it
further_links.summary: Mistral AI has published a strategic document outlining a vision and roadmap for European leadership in artificial intelligence, addressing sovereignty, infrastructure, and competitive positioning.

further_links.title: AI could be the end of the digital wave, not the next big thing
further_links.summary: An analysis drawing on Carlota Perez's technology wave theory argues that AI may represent the concluding phase of the digital era rather than the beginning of a new technological paradigm.

further_links.title: Tech valuations are back to pre-AI boom levels
further_links.summary: Apollo's analysis finds that technology sector valuations have retreated to levels seen before the generative AI investment surge, raising questions about AI's near-term economic impact.
